title: Constance Longitudinal Imaging of Psychosis Treatment Effects: fMRI
summary:
Schizophrenia is a severe mental disorder that is often associated with a chronic course of illness and psychosocial impairments. Patients suffer not only from diagnostically relevant psychotic symptoms, such as delusions or hallucinations, but also from cognitive and social deficits. Treatment guidelines for schizophrenia include medication and psychotherapeutic interventions. Despite the application of evidence-based treatment, disease outcome is highly heterogeneous and individual prognosis is difficult. 
In the current project, we plan to assess changes in social cognition and associated neural activity and connectivity in schizophrenia patients in response to in-patient treatment. For this purpose, examination appointments will take place at the beginning of the inpatient stay in a psychosis treatment ward as well as at discharge and 6 months after discharge. Examination procedures include clinical interviews, behavioral measures, heart rate measurement, questionnaires, and MRI or EEG. The aim of the study is to investigate effects of psychotherapy and to develop models that will allow us to predict treatment courses.
conditions: F25;All patients of a psychosis ward of the ZfP Reichenau as well as further patients of the Soteria ward of the ZfP Reichenau.

interventions.name: Patients are examined shortly after admission (T1) and shortly before discharge (T2) by means of interview, questionnaires and a behavioral task.
